rules.title: LA RSO security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords of rent-stabilized units in the City of Los Angeles must pay tenants accrued interest on security deposits, either monthly or yearly, as a direct payment or a rent credit. The landlord must tell the tenant in writing which method it chose.
rules.key_value: Interest paid monthly or annually (not just at end of tenancy); rate set annually by the City (4.32% for 2025)
rules.quoted_span: A tenant shall be given the unpaid accrued interest in the form of either a direct payment or a credit against the tenant’s rent.
rules.effective_date_note: Interest began accruing November 1, 1990, per the quoted code text.
rules.coverage_conditions: Properties subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LARSO).
rules.penalty: Non-compliance can be raised as a defense in eviction proceedings (per the source article).

unverifiable_exemptions: Unit must be subject to the LA Rent Stabilization Ordinance (exemptions such as single-family homes, condos and post-1978 buildings cannot be verified from parcel data)

parsed.doc_summary: AAGLA article explaining that LA RSO landlords must pay security deposit interest monthly or annually under LAMC 151.06.02, with the written-notice requirement and an annual interest rate table through 2025.
